clue.text: What fiddler might do? Behave obsequiously

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: a violinist bows the instrument and scrapes the strings
second meaning: to fawn on someone servilely

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a playful literal picture of a violinist at work; the second is the idiom for grovelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes excessive deference, like a servant bowing low and scraping a foot backwards.

clue.text: Implore second European to cut tree

indicators.note: the pair of letters cuts into the tree, so they are placed inside its name

parts.note: a beech is a tree

explanation.surface: A plea to stop a second European from felling a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech someone is to beg them earnestly, a synonym of implore.

clue.text: Wife and I put pressure on Edward to get cleaned

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so this letter comes before the name

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A couple leaning on Edward until he tidies up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wiped has been cleaned with a cloth, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Story from resident about a pair of rooks

indicators.note: the resident goes around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a native is a resident of a place
R is the chess abbreviation for rook, so two of them give RR

explanation.surface: A tale told by a local about two birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, the same thing as a story.

clue.text: Hate losing parking place

indicators.note: the word for hate gives up a letter, so that letter is removed

parts.note: spite is malice or hatred
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A grumble about losing a parking place.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position, a synonym of place.

clue.text: Embarrassed Socialist confronted

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or socialist
faced means confronted

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician blushing when challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone red-faced is flushed with shame, the visible sign of being embarrassed.

clue.text: Angler may be after this rod

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a freshwater fish an angler might try to catch
second meaning: an old unit of length, also called a rod or pole

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an angler's fishing rod; in fact rod is the old measure of five and a half yards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a common fish sought by fishermen and an old surveying measure equal to a pole.

clue.text: Ruin shoe on a golf course, finally

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog or shoe
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Someone ruining a shoe out on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf course' looks like one phrase, but golf gives G and course only lends its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or wrecking, so as a verb it means to ruin.

clue.text: Drunk is yet to swallow medium Scotch

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take another one inside them
drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker who has yet to down a glass of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky in this drinking scene, but it is the verb meaning to thwart; the anagram of IS YET gives STYIE, which takes in M.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to put an end to it, and to stymie means to obstruct or thwart.

clue.text: Flipping parrots deserved to be split up

indicators.note: flipping the word over turns it end to end

parts.note: to parrot is to mimic, so parrots means apes
rated means merited or deserved

explanation.surface: An exasperated owner whose birds have earned being kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrots' looks like a plural noun for the birds, but it is a verb meaning copies or mimics.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated means divided or parted, the same as split up.

clue.text: Strongly heat pan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cook with intense heat
second meaning: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly

explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking utensil beside the heating, but it is the verb meaning to criticise severely.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both cooking food in high oven heat and savagely criticising someone or something.

clue.text: Make attractive object, and repair on a regular basis

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for making an item appealing by fixing it up from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of repair are E, A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked or loved, to render them attractive or appealing.

clue.text: Throw boot and harm John from America?

indicators.note: throw the letters about and they land in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone hurling a boot to cause damage.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang a john is a toilet; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a john is the toilet, and a bathroom is the polite American word for that room.

clue.text: The woman with German recluse

parts.note: her is a female pronoun, referring to the woman
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A woman accompanying a German who keeps to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone away from society, exactly what a recluse does.

clue.text: Determined lovers staggered editor

indicators.note: staggered means reeling around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Resolute romantics who left an editor reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resolved has made up their mind firmly, a synonym of determined.

clue.text: Student made one fizzy drink

parts.note: L is a learner, as on the L-plate of a student driver

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A student who has made a carbonated drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy drink' reads as one phrase, but fizzy is the anagram signal and drink alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink, an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Defeat with six balls in cricket pitch

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
to pitch a ball is to throw it

explanation.surface: A cricket scene of a bowler working through an over on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like the cricket pitch, but it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a regime is to topple or defeat it.

clue.text: Bags emptied initially with not much rubbish

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: little means not much

explanation.surface: Bin bags emptied with hardly any refuse in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' looks like a noun for the bags' contents, but it is the verb meaning to disparage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish someone's work is to disparage it, which is what belittling means.

clue.text: Spades were found inside and returned

indicators.note: the first letters are found lying inside the word and

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Playing cards discovered and brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: To return a remark is to reply to it, so returned means answered.

clue.text: Is tense with animal on back

indicators.note: in a down clue the animal placed on the rest sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous creature carrying something on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the animal's back, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a campaign is to support or help it, which is to assist.

clue.text: Both ends of palace fixed with American's money

indicators.note: both ends of a word means its first and last letters

parts.note: set means fixed or established
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American paying for a palace's two ends to be repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain before the euro, a form of money.

clue.text: Strict novelist shortly penning finales of the chapter

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the novelist's shortened name holds the other letters
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Jane Austen was an English novelist

indicators.note: the finales of the two words are their last letters

explanation.surface: A stern novelist writing the end of a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTEN loses N to give AUSTE, which pens ER, the last letters of the and chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: An austere person is severe and stern in manner, the same as strict.

clue.text: Wicked criminal dined with pals abandoning area

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so these letters are rearranged
abandoning means the word gives up a letter

explanation.surface: A wicked crook ate with friends and then ditched the place.
explanation.walkthrough: PALS without A gives PLS, which with DINED is rearranged. 'Wicked' looks like it describes the criminal, but here it is slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech wicked means excellent, and splendid means magnificent or excellent.

clue.text: Note variable length with both old and new fabric

parts.note: Y is a letter used for a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A tailor's note on a cloth of varying length, part old and part new.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic material woven into cloth, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Upset postmistress? Not half!

indicators.note: not half of the word is kept: only its back half survives

explanation.surface: A post-office worker who is distressed, with the reply that she certainly is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it tells you to drop the first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress someone is to worry or upset them, a synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Tedium from some taxi unnecessarily turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top, so backwards
some of the letters across the two words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: The boredom of a needless taxi turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a French loanword meaning the same as tedium.

clue.text: Design detailed aircraft

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail removed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: A design for an aircraft drawn up in fine detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'intricate', but read as de-tailed it removes the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a drawing or scheme for something, the same as a design.

clue.text: Appropriate time to tuck into marine mammal?

indicators.note: the letter tucks itself into the animal, placed inside its name

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is a fitting moment for a seal to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective 'fitting', but it is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for yourself without permission, which is to steal.

clue.text: Shout from Spaniard in half-conscious state showing open-mindedness

indicators.note: the shout sits in the state, placed inside its letters

parts.note: a trance is a dazed half-conscious state
olé is the Spanish cry of approval, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A dazed Spaniard calling out who shows a broad-minded attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is willingness to accept views different from one's own, which is open-mindedness.

clue.text: Sometimes I now ache, line dancing

indicators.note: dancing means moving the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: An ageing line dancer admits to the occasional ache.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, now and then, the same as sometimes.
